note: Rav had offended Rabbi Ḥanina by not restarting a Torah reading for him, and for thirteen years Rav came to him every Yom Kippur eve to ask forgiveness, but Rabbi Ḥanina refused. The Gemara asks how Rav could ask more than three times, against the teaching of Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina, and answers that Rav was different. It then asks how Rabbi Ḥanina could refuse, when Rava taught that whoever lets go of his honor is forgiven his sins. The answer: Rabbi Ḥanina had dreamed that Rav was hung on a palm tree, a sign that he would become head of an academy, so he refused to be appeased, so that Rav would go and study Torah in Babylonia.
why: The Gemara has been telling how Rav sought forgiveness from people on Yom Kippur eve; these questions explain why Rav kept asking and why Rabbi Ḥanina kept refusing, before it turns to the laws of confession on that day.
